summary: When Rosh Hashanah fell on Shabbos, the shofar was blown only in the Beis HaMikdash. After it was destroyed, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule to blow where there is a Beis Din.

chunks.en: When the Yom Tov of Rosh
chunks.st: With regard to the Festival day of Rosh HaShana

chunks.en: Hashanah falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: that occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: they would blow the shofar in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: in the Temple they would sound the shofar as usual.

chunks.en: but not in the rest of the country.
chunks.st: However, they would not sound it in the rest of the country outside the Temple.

chunks.en: After the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: After the Temple was destroyed,

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that

chunks.en: that they should blow in every place
chunks.st: the people should sound the shofar on Shabbat in every place

chunks.en: that has a Beis Din.
chunks.st: where there is a court of twenty-three judges.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar said:

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made the rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted this practice

chunks.en: only for Yavneh.
chunks.st: only in Yavne,
chunks.stMore: where the Great Sanhedrin of seventy-one judges resided in his time, but nowhere else.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.en: both Yavneh and every place
chunks.st: He instituted the practice both in Yavne and in any place

chunks.en: that has a Beis Din.
chunks.st: where there is a court.

summary: In the old days, towns near Yerushalayim also blew the shofar on Shabbos, but in Yavneh it was blown only in the Beis Din itself.

chunks.en: And Yerushalayim had one more thing
chunks.st: The mishna adds: And Jerusalem in earlier times had this additional

chunks.en: better than Yavneh:
chunks.st: superiority over Yavne
chunks.stMore: after Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted this practice,

chunks.en: any city that could see Yerushalayim
chunks.st: for in any city whose residents could see Jerusalem

chunks.en: and hear the shofar, and was close, and could come there,
chunks.st: and hear the sounding of the shofar from there, and which was near to Jerusalem and people could come to Jerusalem from there,

chunks.en: they would blow there. But in Yavneh they would blow
chunks.st: they would sound the shofar there as well, as it was considered part of Jerusalem. But in Yavne they would sound the shofar

chunks.en: only in the Beis Din.
chunks.st: only in the court itself, not in the surrounding cities.

summary: After the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made rules to remember it, like taking the lulav all seven days of Sukkos everywhere.
stIntro: After the previous mishna mentioned Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai’s ordinance that applies to the sounding of the shofar, this mishna records other ordinances instituted by the same Sage:

chunks.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה הַלּוּלָב נִטָּל בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ שִׁבְעָה,
chunks.en: At first, the lulav was taken in the Beis HaMikdash for seven days,
chunks.st: At first, during the Temple era, the lulav was taken in the Temple all seven days of Sukkot,

chunks.en: and in the rest of the country for one day.
chunks.st: and in the rest of the country outside the Temple, it was taken only one day, on the first day of the Festival.

chunks.en: After the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: After the Temple was destroyed,

chunks.he: הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי שֶׁיְהֵא
chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that

chunks.he: לוּלָב נִטָּל בַּמְּדִינָה שִׁבְעָה זֵכֶר לַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
chunks.en: that the lulav be taken in the country for seven days, to remember the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: the lulav should be taken even in the rest of the country all seven days, in commemoration of the Temple.

chunks.en: and that on the whole day of waving the omer, new grain is forbidden.
chunks.explain: New grain may not be eaten all that day.
chunks.st: And for similar reasons, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that for the entire day of waving the omer offering, i.e., the sixteenth of Nisan, eating the grain of the new crop is prohibited.
chunks.stMore: By Torah law, when the Temple is standing the new grain may not be eaten until after the omer offering is brought on the sixteenth of Nisan, usually early in the morning. When the Temple is not standing it may be eaten from the time that the eastern horizon is illuminated at daybreak. However, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted a prohibition against eating the new grain throughout the entire sixteenth of Nisan, until the seventeenth, to commemorate the Temple.

words.note: The day the omer was waved, the sixteenth of Nisan.

summary: At first, witnesses for the new moon were accepted all day, but after a mix-up with the Leviim's song, only until Minchah. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai changed this back, and made another rule too.

chunks.en: At first, they would accept witnesses
chunks.st: Initially, they would accept testimony to determine the start

chunks.en: for the new moon all day long.
chunks.st: of the month throughout the entire thirtieth day
chunks.stMore: from the beginning of the month of Elul, before Rosh HaShana, and if witnesses arrived from afar and testified that they had sighted the New Moon the previous night, they would declare that day the Festival.

chunks.en: Once, the witnesses were late in coming,
chunks.st: Once, the witnesses tarried coming until the hour was late,

chunks.en: and the Leviim made a mistake in their song.
chunks.explain: They did not know if it was Yom Tov or a weekday.
chunks.st: and the Levites erred with regard to the song,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the psalm that they were supposed to recite, as they did not know at the time whether it was a Festival or an ordinary weekday.

chunks.en: So they made a rule that they would accept witnesses
chunks.st: From that point on, the Sages instituted that they would accept testimony to determine the start of the month

chunks.en: only until Minchah time.
chunks.st: only until minḥa
chunks.stMore: time. If witnesses had not arrived by that hour, they would declare Elul a thirty-day month and calculate the dates of the Festivals accordingly.

chunks.he: וְאִם בָּאוּ עֵדִים מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה,
chunks.en: And if witnesses came from Minchah time on,
chunks.st: And if witnesses came from minḥa time onward,
chunks.stMore: although the calculations for the dates of the Festivals would begin from the following day, the people would nevertheless

chunks.he: נוֹהֲגִין אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם קֹדֶשׁ וּלְמָחָר קֹדֶשׁ.
chunks.en: they kept that day holy, and the next day holy too.
chunks.st: observe that day, on which the witnesses arrived, as sacred, so that in future years they would not treat the entire day as a weekday and engage in labor from the morning on the assumption that the witnesses will arrive only after minḥa time. And they would also observe the following day as sacred.
chunks.stMore: On the second day, they observed Rosh HaShana in full, both by sacrificing its offerings as well as by calculating the upcoming Festivals from that date.

chunks.en: After the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: After the Temple was destroyed
chunks.stMore: and there was no longer any reason for this ordinance,

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted

chunks.he: שֶׁיְּהוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ כָּל הַיּוֹם.
chunks.en: that they would accept witnesses for the new moon all day long.
chunks.st: that they would once again accept testimony to determine the start of the month the entire day.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said:

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
chunks.st: And this, too, Rabban

chunks.en: also made this rule:
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין בְּכָל מָקוֹם,
chunks.en: that even if the head of the Beis Din is somewhere else,
chunks.st: that even if the head of the court of seventy-one is in any other place, not where the Great Sanhedrin is in session,

chunks.en: the witnesses should go
chunks.st: the witnesses should nevertheless go

chunks.en: only to the place where the Beis Din gathers.
chunks.st: only to the place where the Great Sanhedrin gathers
chunks.stMore: to deliver testimony to determine the start of the month. Although the date of the month is dependent on the head of the Great Sanhedrin, as it is he who declares that the month is sanctified (see 24a), nevertheless, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that the members of the Great Sanhedrin may sanctify the month in the absence of the head of the court.

summary: This mishnah teaches the order of the brachos in Musaf of Rosh Hashanah, with Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros, and where the shofar is blown. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and Rabbi Akiva disagree about where Malchiyos goes.

chunks.en: The order of the brachos:
chunks.st: The order of the blessings
chunks.stMore: of the additional prayer on Rosh HaShana is as follows:

chunks.en: He says Avos, Gevuros, and Kedushas Hashem,
chunks.st: One recites the blessing of the Patriarchs, the blessing of God’s Mighty Deeds, and the blessing of the Sanctification of God’s Name, all of which are recited all year long.

words.note: The first bracha of Shemoneh Esrei, about our fathers.
The second bracha, about Hashem's mighty deeds.

chunks.en: and he puts Malchiyos together with them,
chunks.st: And one includes the blessing of Kingship, containing many biblical verses on that theme, with them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in the blessing of the Sanctification of God’s Name,

chunks.en: and he does not blow the shofar.
chunks.st: and he does not sound the shofar after it.

chunks.en: Then Kedushas HaYom,
chunks.st: Next, one adds a special blessing for the Sanctification of the Day,

chunks.en: and he blows. Then Zichronos,
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it; followed by the blessing of Remembrances,
chunks.stMore: which contains many biblical verses addressing that theme,

chunks.en: and he blows. Then Shofaros,
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it; and recites the blessing of Shofarot,
chunks.stMore: which includes verses that mention the shofar,

chunks.he: וְתוֹקֵעַ. וְאוֹמֵר עֲבוֹדָה וְהוֹדָאָה וּבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים,
chunks.en: and he blows. Then he says Avodah, Hodaah, and Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it. And he then returns to the regular Amida prayer and recites the blessing of God’s Service and the blessing of Thanksgiving and the Priestly Blessing.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: "If he does not blow for Malchiyos,
chunks.st: If one does not sound the shofar for the blessing of Kingship,

chunks.en: why does he say it there?
chunks.st: why does he mention it?

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר אָבוֹת וּגְבוּרוֹת וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם,
chunks.en: Rather, he says Avos, Gevuros, and Kedushas Hashem,
chunks.st: Rather, the order of the blessings is as follows: One recites the blessing of the Patriarchs and that of God’s Mighty Deeds and that of the Sanctification of God’s Name.

chunks.en: and puts Malchiyos together with Kedushas HaYom,
chunks.st: He subsequently includes the blessing of Kingship in the blessing of the Sanctification of the Day,

chunks.en: and he blows. Then Zichronos,
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar. Next he recites the blessing of Remembrances,

chunks.en: and he blows. Then Shofaros,
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it, and the blessing of Shofarot

chunks.he: וְתוֹקֵעַ. וְאוֹמֵר עֲבוֹדָה וְהוֹדָאָה וּבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים:
chunks.en: and he blows. Then he says Avodah, Hodaah, and Birkas Kohanim."
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it. He then recites the blessing of God’s Service and the blessing of Thanksgiving and the Priestly Blessing.

summary: In each of Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros we say ten pesukim, starting from the Torah and ending with the Nevi'im. We do not use pesukim about punishment.

chunks.en: We do not say fewer than ten pesukim of Malchiyos,
chunks.st: One does not recite fewer than ten verses in theblessing of Kingship,

chunks.en: or fewer than ten of Zichronos,
chunks.st: or fewer than ten verses in the blessing of Remembrances,

chunks.en: or fewer than ten of Shofaros.
chunks.st: or fewer than ten verses in the blessing of Shofarot.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says:

chunks.en: "If he said three of each one,
chunks.st: If one recited three from each of them,

chunks.en: he has done the mitzvah." We do not say pesukim of Zichronos, Malchiyos,
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation. One does not mention verses of Remembrance, Kingship,

chunks.en: or Shofaros that are about punishment.
chunks.st: and Shofar that have a theme of punishment.

chunks.en: He starts with the Torah and ends with the Navi.
chunks.st: When reciting the ten verses, one begins with verses from the Torah and concludes with verses from the Prophets.

words.note: The books of the Nevi'im, the Prophets.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: "If he ended with the Torah, he has done the mitzvah."
chunks.st: If he concluded with a verse from the Torah, he has fulfilled his obligation.

summary: On Rosh Hashanah, the chazzan of Musaf is the one who has the shofar blown. On days with Hallel, the chazzan of Shacharis says Hallel.

chunks.en: The chazzan who leads the davening on the Yom Tov
chunks.st: With regard to one who is passing before the ark, as prayer leader,

words.note: The place where the chazzan stands.

chunks.en: of Rosh Hashanah:
chunks.st: on the festival of Rosh HaShana,

chunks.en: the second one has the shofar blown.
chunks.st: it is the second prayer leader, i.e., the one who leads the additional prayer, who sounds the shofar on behalf of the congregation.

chunks.en: And at the time of Hallel,
chunks.st: And on a day when the hallel is recited,

chunks.en: the first one leads Hallel.
chunks.st: the first prayer leader, i.e., the one who leads the morning prayer, recites the hallel on behalf of the congregation.

summary: We may not break the rules of Shabbos or Yom Tov to get a shofar ready for Rosh Hashanah. Children may blow the shofar to learn, and one must blow with the mitzvah in mind.

chunks.en: For the shofar of Rosh Hashanah,
chunks.st: With regard to the shofar of Rosh HaShana,

chunks.en: we may not walk past the Shabbos limit for it,
chunks.st: one may not pass the Shabbat limit for it, i.e., to go and hear it,

words.note: The Shabbos limit: how far one may walk out of town.

chunks.en: and we may not clear away a pile of stones for it.
chunks.st: nor may one clear a pile of rubble to uncover a buried shofar.

chunks.en: We may not climb a tree,
chunks.st: One may not climb a tree,

chunks.en: or ride on an animal,
chunks.st: nor may one ride on an animal,

chunks.en: or swim in the water.
chunks.st: nor may one swim in water, in order to find a shofar to sound.

chunks.en: And we may not cut it, whether
chunks.st: And one may not cut the shofar to prepare it for use,

chunks.en: with something the Rabbis forbade,
chunks.st: neither with an object that is prohibited due to a rabbinic decree

words.note: Shevus: something the Rabbis forbade on Shabbos and Yom Tov.

chunks.he: וּבֵין בְּדָבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
chunks.en: or with something the Torah forbids.
chunks.st: nor with an object that may not be used due to a prohibition by Torah law.

chunks.en: But if he wants to put
chunks.st: However, if one wishes to place

chunks.en: water or wine into it,
chunks.st: water or wine into
chunks.stMore: the shofar on Rosh HaShana so that it emits a clear sound,

chunks.he: יִתֵּן. אֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַתִּינוֹקוֹת מִלִּתְקוֹעַ,
chunks.en: he may put it. We do not stop children from blowing,
chunks.st: he may place it, as this does not constitute a prohibited labor. One need not prevent children from sounding
chunks.stMore: the shofar on Rosh HaShana, despite the fact that they are not obligated in mitzvot.

chunks.en: but we help them until they learn.
chunks.st: Rather, one occupies himself with them, encouraging and instructing them, until they learn how to sound it properly.

chunks.en: Someone who blows without meaning to do the mitzvah has not done it,
chunks.st: The mishna adds: One who acts unawares and sounds the shofar without any intention to perform the mitzva has not fulfilled his obligation.

words.en: and one who is just blowing
words.note: Blowing without meaning to do the mitzvah.

chunks.en: and someone who hears it from him
chunks.st: And, similarly, one who hears the shofar blasts from one who acts unawares

chunks.en: has not done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: has not fulfilled his obligation.

summary: This mishnah teaches the order and length of the shofar blasts. It also teaches that every person must daven Musaf, while Rabban Gamliel says the chazzan does it for everyone.

chunks.en: The order of the blasts
chunks.st: The order of the blasts

chunks.en: is three sets of three each.
chunks.st: is three sets of three blasts each, which are: Tekia, terua, and tekia.

chunks.en: A tekiah is as long as three teruos.
chunks.st: The length of a tekia is equal to the length of three teruot,

chunks.en: A teruah is as long as three crying sounds.
chunks.st: and the length of a terua is equal to the length of three whimpers.

chunks.en: If he blew the first tekiah,
chunks.st: If one sounded the first
chunks.stMore: tekia of the initial series of tekia, terua, tekia,

chunks.en: and made the second one as long as two,
chunks.st: and then extended the second tekia of that series to the length of two
chunks.stMore: tekiot, so that it should count as both the second tekia of the first set and the first tekia of the second set,

chunks.en: it counts as only one.
chunks.st: he has in his hand the fulfillment of only one
chunks.stMore: tekia, and he must begin the second set with a new tekia.

chunks.en: Someone who said the brachos, and afterward
chunks.st: With regard to one who recited the blessings of the additional prayer, and only afterward

chunks.en: got a shofar,
chunks.st: a shofar became available to him,

chunks.en: blows tekiah, teruah, tekiah three times.
chunks.st: he sounds a tekia, sounds a terua, and sounds a tekia, an order he repeats three times.

chunks.en: Just as the chazzan must daven,
chunks.st: Just as the prayer leader is obligated in the prayer of Rosh HaShana,

chunks.en: so every single person must daven.
chunks.st: so too, each and every individual is obligated in these prayers.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel disagrees and says:

chunks.en: The chazzan does the mitzvah
chunks.st: Individuals are not obligated, as the prayer leader fulfills the obligation

chunks.en: for everyone.
chunks.st: on behalf of the many.
